page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured for compute-heavy artificial intelligence workloads and parallel data processing. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor featuring 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture without hyperthreading, alongside 180 GB of system memory delivering 11.25 GB per core. Acceleration is anchored by a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. High-speed local persistence is supplied via a bundled 1200 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional machine learning inference capabilities. In LLM evaluations, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing throughput of 13,631.52 tokens per second and generation throughput of 610.8 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, alongside 6,293.73 prompt tokens per second and 153.1 generation tokens per second on 7B models. Compute benchmarks place Geekbench single-core performance at 2,130.0 and text processing at 2,843.0, both ranking in the top percentiles. Decompression throughput via bzip3 also ranks in the top tier at 15.59 GB per second single-threaded.

General-purpose CPU metrics reflect balanced mid-range behavior, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 40,930.36, stress-ng multi-core throughput of 34,834.61, and Redis operations reaching 41.33 million operations per second. Hardware vector extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16 support dense numerical pipelines, although AMX is unavailable. Large-block memory writes measure 66.7 GB per second.

The 11.25 GB per core memory allocation combined with 48 GB of high-speed GPU memory delivers strong resource density for small-to-medium large language model inference, fine-tuning, image generation pipelines, and memory-intensive analytical processing.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by a 16-core Intel Xeon 6448H processor running at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture, paired with 180 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by an NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM, supported by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier inference speeds for small and medium language models, delivering over 6,290 prompt tokens per second on 7B architectures. Instruction set support includes AVX-512, BF16, and VNNI for accelerated matrix arithmetic. General CPU tasks perform in the median range, with 41.33 million Redis operations per second and steady multi-core execution. With an elevated memory-to-core ratio of 11.25 GB per core, this instance is suited for AI inference serving, model fine-tuning, image synthesis, and data-intensive visual computing.
